reason: Verification shows the simulation is syntactically solid but fails core specification compliance: missing entities (Household, Location, Retailer, Government, MediaChannel, SocialNetwork as first-class), movement/enforcement, supply/purchasing, and required metrics/parameters. With three iterations left, there is clear room for significant improvement by implementing a minimal but spec-aligned feature set (small-world network, policy signal decoupling, awareness decay, basic supply/purchasing, movement/enforcement, and contextual/inequality metrics).

specific_areas: Introduce minimal spec-aligned entities: Household, Location (with policy/enforcement), Retailer (inventory, price, restock with lead time), Government, MediaChannel, and a SocialNetwork wrapper
Implement a Watts–Strogatz small-world topology controlled by social_network_type and ws_rewiring_p
Decouple policy signal from trust and add awareness_decay; ensure policy has a floor effect
Add movement scheduler using location_mix; assign each agent a daily context and apply per-Location enforcement and fines
Add minimal purchasing/supply: Person/Household mask_inventory, purchase attempts with price_elasticity and income, retailer stock/stockouts, restocking pipeline

Expand DEFAULT_PARAM_DEFS to include spec parameters (time_step_hours, media_campaign_intensity, misinformation_rate, enforcement_strength, fine_amount, price_elasticity, retailer_restock_rate, supply_lead_time_days, initial_inventory_per_capita, location_mix, disease_incidence_signal, risk_perception_sensitivity, comfort_penalty, compliance_cost_disutility)
Integrate risk_perception dynamics into adoption decision using disease_incidence_signal
Extend metrics: contextual_adoption_rate by location, inequality_index across SES/age, stockout_frequency, and a simple policy_effect_size estimate
Guard calibrator file writes with SKIP_IO and remove redundant pass statements

task_understanding.adjustments: Maintain a checklist mapping each spec requirement to code artifacts (entities, parameters, interactions, metrics). Treat missing entities and interactions as blockers for this iteration.

data_analysis.adjustments: Define inputs/signals for disease_incidence_signal and media/misinformation rates; prepare simple synthetic profiles for location_mix and SES/income distributions to enable inequality and contextual metrics without external data.

model_planning.adjustments: Produce a minimal architecture plan: (1) Entities stubs; (2) Daily loop order: policy/media -> movement -> purchasing -> enforcement -> adoption -> aggregation -> restock updates; (3) Acceptance tests: classes exist, parameters recognized, small-world degree/path-length sanity checks, metrics keys produced.

code_generation.adjustments: Implement in small, testable increments: add entity classes and interfaces first; wire in network construction; then movement/enforcement; then purchasing/supply; finally metrics. Use parameter guards and sensible defaults to avoid breaking existing runs.

code_verification.adjustments: Add unit-level checks: network small-world properties (average clustering/path length within expected bounds for sample N), SKIP_IO guard in calibrators, presence and ranges of new parameters, and non-empty contextual metrics. Run quick smoke simulations to ensure no runtime errors.

simulation_execution.adjustments: Introduce time-budget guards around new steps; ensure daily step works with time_step_hours=24. Log (in-memory) counts for stockouts and enforcement actions for aggregator consumption without I/O.

result_evaluation.adjustments: Verify contextual_adoption_rate, inequality_index, stockout_frequency, and policy_effect_size are populated and stable over short runs. Compare adoption curves with/without enforcement/media to confirm qualitative responsiveness.

feedback_generation.adjustments: Provide a spec-traceable summary in the next report: which entities/interactions/parameters/metrics were added, with code pointers and any remaining gaps deferred to the following iteration.
